text: 2026-10-01 ScalaFIM-side prerequisites done, local commit 7d0ac861cdd24e1717521d9b18faaef1d7df3b80 on work/fslr-lattice-inverse-20261001 (not pushed or merged). (1) All-vertex independent oracle: tools/transform/generate_fslr_inverse_oracle.py, SimpleITK 2.5.6 on the original HDF5 composite. Fixed point from identity, no lattice. All 64,984 vertices converge to <= 1e-10 mm (at most 33 iterations), all inside support. It reproduces the committed 2500-vertex fixture within 4x each recorded residual (max ratio 0.39); output is deterministic. RealInverseOracleSuite: ITK solutions round-trip through ScalaFIM's exact declared map <= 1e-6 mm at every vertex. (2) Consumer-agnostic FslrBridgeDisagreement runner. The consumer fixtures (3 beta + 12 FIR brain-direction maps, 2 mm 2009c grid) are supplied through specs outside the repo; results are in /private/tmp/scalafim-fslr-inverse-20261001-evidence/disagreement-lattice-{beta,fir}.json. Lattice candidate vs oracle, per hemisphere (about 29.7k cortical vertices): placement max 0.088 / 0.067 mm; voxel disagreements 106 / 107 (0.36%); support (coverage) disagreements 1 / 4; value disagreements 94 / 97 per map; max value change 1.6-4.0 SD of the map's cortical values; sign flips 12-30 per map. This confirms the review: boundary voxel flips have material value, sign and support effects on real maps, so the route stays unavailable. Implication for upstream qualification: nearest-voxel lookup is discontinuous, so the pointwise inverse must agree with the oracle to the oracle's convergence level (voxel/support/value disagreements ~0, not merely small placement error). Value-level disagreement on the consumer fixtures should become a frozen budget before evaluating the pointwise candidate. RealLatticeInverseSuite is now opt-in (it wedged the sbt server). Gates: surfaceJVM/test 280 passed / 5 opt-in skipped, surfaceJS/test 224 / 1 existing skip, no warnings.
